sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European-derived, with commercial and maritime influences)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–Spain Reciprocal Protection of Investments Treaty (2000)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 on AML/CFT (as amended); Executive Decree No. 92 of 2015; Law No. 70 of 30 September 2021 creating the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Register; Directive rules of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney (POA) for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public or foreign notary under the Hague Apostille Convention
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama; if non-Hague jurisdiction, consular legalization at the Panamanian Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled Articles of Incorporation / Pacto Social and Bylaws (Estatutos)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled UBO Declaration (Declaración del Beneficiario Final) under Law 70 of 2021
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) through the SIRCE/UBO module or licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the Panamanian National Police (BP) PEP list, the Panamanian UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) internal risk indicators, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the U.S. OFAC SDN list, and the EU consolidated financial sanctions list. Screening is performed at onboarding and renewed annually for this low-risk online retail entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIRCE (Sistema de Registro de Comercio Electrónico) of the Registro Público de Panamá
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Spanish or any language using the Latin script; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into a Latin-script equivalent prior to registration. The corporate ending must be 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' and the name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered entity name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 business days after a name rejection notice, the applicant may file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá, and in the alternative a 'Recurso de Apelación' to the Junta Directiva of the Registro Público within 5 business days if the reconsideration is denied. The appeal must state the legal grounds, request the contested name, and attach any supporting consent or distinguishing argument. The Registry must resolve within 30 days; ultimate judicial review is available before the Third Administrative Court of the Contencioso-Administrativo.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible as the general statutory address only if the licensed registered agent maintains a physical local panamanian address and remains available for service of process; the company itself may operate entirely remotely, which is standard for an online cosmetics retail business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk; for a non-regulated, low-risk online cosmetics retail entity, the estimated probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by registry authorities in the first year is less than 5%. AML regulators may occasionally audit the registered agent's compliance files for adherence to Law 23 and Law 70.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance certificate (SIRCE filing)
Notarization of incorporation documents (Pacto Social, Bylaws, UBO declaration signatures)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed notarial fee under prevailing Panamanian market rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry incorporation filing and initial registration of Sociedad Anónima
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry fee based on authorized capital; minimum capital tolerated

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille of the three-document notarization and compliance bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official governmental fee per apostille (three documents)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered Agent and Commercial Domicile service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market benchmark for registered agency compliance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO Register filing under Law 70 of 2021
AML/PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening and compliance setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified compliance provider or licensed law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee for online PEP and sanctions screening of directors and UBOs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence, drafting of incorporation resolutions, and corporate record book preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Lead counsel (custodian law firm in Panama)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed legal fee for pre-incorporation due diligence and statutory incorporation documentation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 32 of 26 February 1927 (General Law on Joint-Stock Corporations, 'Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas'), as amended by Law 5 of 2015 and Law 4 of 2015, applicable to the standard Panama Sociedad Anónima; key provisions include Arts. 1–14 (incorporation by public deed, corporate purpose, capital structure) and Art. 20 (registered office and resident agent requirement).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Mercantile Section (Sección de Personas Jurídicas / Sociedades), acting after notarization by a Panamanian Notary Public (Notaría Pública).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pública Escritura de Constitución (notarized public deed of incorporation) submitted for mercantile registration, together with the corresponding registry fee receipt.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists for a standard S.A.; the Articles fix the authorized capital (commonly US$10,000) and the initial subscribed/paid-up capital (commonly one share of US$100 nominal value). No bank escrow account or capital deposit requirement is imposed by Law 32 of 1927.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], S.A. RESOLVED, that the directors accept the subscription for 100 ordinary shares at US$1.00 par value per share, paid in cash, and register the subscribers as shareholders in the Company's share ledger. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at [Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and that the licensed registered agent be retained to maintain the legal address and corporate records. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] appointed Secretary and [Name] appointed Treasurer, each holding office until the next shareholders' meeting, with authority to execute contracts, open and operate bank accounts in the Republic of Panama and abroad, and engage external accounting and tax advisers. Adopted unanimously by the directors on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registro / EDEBE online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-search petition ('Certificado de Nombre') through the EDEBE platform or in person at the Public Registry, selecting a name that is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity; pay the search fee; the registry issues a non-transferable name availability certificate valid for a limited period.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, file a written reconsideration with the Registry's name office or re-apply with a distinctive alternate name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (Panamanian Notary Public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Panamanian attorney to draft the Pública Escritura de Constitución setting forth the corporate name, corporate purpose (including online retail of cosmetics and personal care products under ISIC 4791), authorized/subscribed/paid-up capital, classes and par value of shares, shareholder rights, board composition, registered office address and first officer appointments; the incorporators execute the deed before the Notary, who attests it and issues certified testimonies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation and By-laws (Estatutos)
Passports or identity cards of incorporators
Anti-money-laundering source-of-funds forms for professional service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies formal defects, convene the parties to correct signature or content errors; post-signature deficiencies may be cured by a notarial clarification instrument (aclaratoria) before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Tesorería / EDEBE fee module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate and pay the proportional inscription fee based on the authorized capital (inclusive of stamp and certified-copy fees) through the EDEBE electronic gateway or a Banco Nacional de Panamá deposit; obtain a stamped payment voucher referencing the deed number for submission with the incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Notarial testimony of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If underpayment is detected, pay the assessed difference and surcharge within the Registry's notified term; verify the applicable tariff code before payment to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile registration with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantile Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original notarized testimony of the Public Deed of Incorporation together with the fee receipt and the completed registry declaration form; the Registrar verifies compliance with Law 32 of 1927, records the corporation, and issues the certified inscription ('Certificado de Personería Jurídica' / registered copy) evidencing the company's legal existence.
required_dossiers: Notarized Public Deed of Incorporation (Pública Escritura de Constitución)
Completed registry declaration form (Movimiento de Sociedades)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns the document for defects, cure the observed deficiency through a notarial amendment and re-present the instrument; unresolved queries may be appealed to the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of initial corporate governance and registered agent arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the Company / licensed resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the First Board Resolution approving the share subscription, adoption of the registered office, and appointment of the President, Secretary and Treasurer; the licensed registered agent (fiduciary or law firm) records the officer appointments in the corporate minute book and share ledger, and issues compliance certificates for banking and tax onboarding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer declines or resigns, hold an extraordinary board meeting and record a replacement resolution in the minutes; no separate registry filing is required for officers unless the deed expressly mandates it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and operating notice (RUC and Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Municipalidad de Panamá (Dirección de Patentes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) application with DGI through the online SIE/Tax portal, attaching the certified incorporation copy and director/legal representative identification; submit the Aviso de Operación notice and obtain the municipal commercial patent if a physical office is maintained; the resulting registration enables e-commerce invoicing, bank account opening and payment-rail onboarding with Shopify Payments and PayPal.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Deed (Personería Jurídica)
Corporate name, commercial address and ISIC 4791 activity description
Identity documents of directors and legal representative
Aviso de Operación form and municipal license application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI queries the activity code or address, resubmit with the detailed ISIC 4791 e-commerce description and lease/utility proof; late-filing penalties may be mitigated by voluntarily filing the Aviso de Operación with supporting documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Ventanilla Única de Inversiones; Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for the Aviso de Operación; Municipality of Panama for the commercial patent; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección de Regulación y Fiscalización for cosmetic product sanitary notification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) issued by DGI and Patente Municipal (Commercial Patent) issued by the local Municipality; for beauty retail, a 'Notificación Sanitaria de Productos Cosméticos' under MINSA applies to each commercialized cosmetic, plus the e-commerce registration of the digital storefront.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Low-Impact Operations. Pure online retail of cosmetics (no manufacturing, no hazardous storage) falls within the low-impact registration tier and is ordinarily exempt from a full Environmental Impact Study (EsIA); a simplified environmental form (Diagnóstico Ambiental / Registro de Actividad de Bajo Impacto) is recommended before opening a warehouse.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions arise in pure online retail; any warehouse/office discharging sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer permit parameters (pH 6–9, TSS, BOD5) per national environmental regulations. Solid waste and packaging must be managed in accordance with MiAMBIENTE's waste-management rules and Panama's extended-producer-responsibility requirements for imported packaged cosmetics; returned/expired cosmetic products must be segregated and disposed as special waste, not via domestic drainage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (fire code inspection covering exits, extinguishers and electrical load); structural load inspection by the Municipal Engineering Directorate if racked storage or mezzanine shelving is installed; occupational health and workplace clearance under MITRADEL health-and-safety rules, including emergency lighting, first aid, personal protective equipment for warehouse staff, and hygiene protocols for handling cosmetics.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de la República de Panamá; Sede Electrónica: https://sede.dgi.gob.pa; Portal informativo: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity intending to engage in Panamanian sitused trade must (1) appoint a resident legal representative with DGI-recognized powers, (2) obtain or rely on a Panama Sociedad Anónima incorporation certificate filed in the Registro Público, (3) execute and notarize a power of attorney in favor of the representative, (4) register the address of the local registered office, (5) submit Formulario de Inscripción en el Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) through the DGI Sede Electrónica, and (6) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación before any taxable activity. DGI issues a provisional RUC immediately upon registration; definitive RUC follows after validation and physical inspection where required. Invoices may only be issued once the RUC appears as 'activo' in the DGI registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election, no hybrid mismatch election, and no voluntary entity-classification regime exists under Panamanian law. A Panama Sociedad Anónima is per se a juristic entity taxed at entity level exclusively on Panamanian-source income. Foreign shareholders do not alter this classification. Special regimes such as tax-privileged Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) and certain multinational licenses are statutory regimes, not election-against-default classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (VAT/GST equivalent)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.0 — no monetary threshold. Registration in the RUC is mandatory for any person or entity engaged on a habitual basis in taxable transfers, imports, or services situated in Panama. Small taxpayers with annual gross income not exceeding B/.150,000 may qualify for a simplified quarterly remittance mechanism without relief from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory authorisation-based electronic invoicing applies to all RUC-active taxpayers. Invoices must be transcribed into DGI's electronic system as structured XML using approved digital certificates, carry an electronic authorization number and/or QR stamp, and be transmitted to the DGI platform by the next business day after issuance. Export invoices require pre-validation through the DGI export submodule. API/web-service integration is mandatory for enterprise taxpayers; smaller taxpayers may use DGI's free web portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0% ITBMS) applies to movable goods physically removed from Panama under a valid customs export declaration, provided the sale is conditioned upon export and title passes to a foreign buyer. Offshore services qualify if the benefit, performance, and use occur entirely outside Panama and the recipient is a non-resident. Cosmetic and personal-care retail products must satisfy the same documentary test as general merchandise, including proof of delivery to a foreign address and receipt of funds from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — DUCA (Declaración Única de Aduana para Exportación)
Commercial invoice expressly stating 'Exportación a 0% ITBMS'
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or international freight manifest evidencing departure from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/IBDC credit evidence in the name of the exporting entity
Certificate of Origin where preferential tariff treatment is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may retrospectively recharacterise an export as taxable local sale if any element of the documentary chain is inconsistent, unverifiable, or not received before the audit closing date. The taxpayer bears the burden of proof. Consequences include a 7% ITBMS clawback computed on the invoice value, statutory monthly surcharges compounded up to 50%, fines up to B/.5,000 for false invoicing, business-closure orders, and criminal liability for fraudulent zero-rating declarations. Retroactive assessment generally covers the applicable five-year statute of limitations from the date of invoice issuance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) — Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized economy with the US Dollar as legal tender; there is no central bank issuing domestic currency and no foreign exchange control law. Capital account transactions and current account profit remittances are unrestricted for foreign-owned entities, subject only to standard AML/KYC bank-level compliance. Dividends paid by a Panamanian corporation to non-resident shareholders are generally not subject to Panamanian income tax under the territorial tax system, provided the underlying income was derived from foreign sources and not from Panama-sourced activities. Repatriation is executed via normal US-dollar wire transfers without SBP approval. Practical hurdles are limited to bank due-diligence documentation for outward remittances above compliance thresholds and the absence of a domestic lender of last resort, which elevates the importance of correspondent banking relationships.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements in Panama. Exporters are not obliged to convert, deposit, or repatriate foreign currency earnings within any timeline. All transactions may be settled in US dollars or any freely convertible currency, and proceeds can be retained offshore or in any local bank account at the company's discretion. The only applicable obligation is the general AML/CFT requirement to maintain accurate books and records of cross-border wire movements under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / POS and Business Account
Operational Account / Escrow and Trade Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — High with structure. Panama has no dedicated EMI licensing regime for non-bank digital payment institutions; the SBP regulates payment systems and Payment Service Providers under the Ley de Sistemas de Pagos. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK FCA-authorized, EU-licensed EMIs, or US money transmitters) may serve as auxiliary collection/settlement accounts for cross-border e-commerce receivables, but they cannot replace a Panamanian bank account for statutory corporate substance, tax residency, or transaction record-keeping. Legal constraints include: (i) no SBP sandbox for foreign EMIs without a domestic banking license; (ii) EMIs often reject Panama-domiciled S.A. clients due to perceived LATAM/offshore risk; (iii) incoming proceeds to an EMI and onward transfer to Panama may trigger enhanced due diligence under FATF-style wire transfer rules; (iv) a Panama S.A. cannot open a corporate account with most EU/UK EMIs without a local director or UBO passport, utility bill, and source-of-funds evidence. Recommended structure: use the Panamanian S.A. as the principal seller-of-record with a local Tier 1 bank account, and use an EMI (e.g., Payoneer, Airwallex, or Dlocal) only as a collection sweep rail from marketplaces like Amazon, Shopify, or TikTok Shop, subject to monthly sweep to the Panama corporate account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panama's SBP does not codify a general statutory requirement that all directors must appear physically at the bank. In practice, Tier 1 Panamanian banks require at least one signatory director or authorized officer to attend an in-person due-diligence interview at the branch; non-signatory directors may remain remote. Remote opening is available at a minority of banks (e.g., Towerbank's digital onboarding for non-Panamanian clients) but generally requires apostilled corporate documents, notarized powers of attorney, and a video or Skype call with compliance officers. For the PA_CORP S.A. with non-resident ownership, the prudent baseline is: (i) physical appearance of one appointed director with passport and proof of address; (ii) apostilled Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation (Poderes), and Board Resolution; (iii) passport copies of all directors/shareholders above 10%; (iv) a current original utility bill or bank statement for each signatory; and (v) a sworn source-of-funds statement signed in the presence of a notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Panama S.A. with bearer shares or opaque ownership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provision of (i) updated share register (Registro de Accionistas) filed with the Registro Público; (ii) sworn declaration that no bearer shares exist; (iii) notarized and apostilled Certificate of Good Standing; (iv) personal identification and source-of-wealth documentation for all UBOs above 10%; (v) a signed AML compliance attestation accepting the bank's due-diligence terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors/managers without tax ID or local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the corporate license and Panama Tax ID (RUC) if registered; (ii) proof of registered agent (Resident Agent) engaged under Law 52 of 2016; (iii) Board Resolution confirming commercial purpose in online retail; (iv) a notarized declaration of the entity's foreign-source income model; (v) signed Form S-15/S-17 if applying for a tax certificate; (vi) annual corporate income tax return history to evidence good standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume e-commerce receipts from fragmented cross-border PSPs (PayPal/Shopify) triggering unexplained wealth red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A forensic treasury file comprising (i) platform KYC evidence and settlement statements from Shopify Payments and PayPal; (ii) a reconciled cash-flow ledger mapping each inbound transfer to a customer order ID and market; (iii) the entity's website/storefront URL and supplier invoices; (iv) sales tax/ITBMS registration (código de registro) if Panama-sourced sales occur; (v) a signed auditor's letter or CPA-prepared financial statement covering the transaction period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions routed via high-risk jurisdictions or sanctioned counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade-partner shielding file: (i) OFAC/SDN screening reports for all counterparties and beneficial owners; (ii) negative media reports from World-Check or LexisNexis; (iii) commercial invoices and contracts evidencing the underlying trade; (iv) copies of the passport and residency proof for the ultimate supplier/manufacturer; (v) a written statement that no transactions involve Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Venezuela, or sanctioned Crimea regions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid deposit-and-sweep liquidity pattern through EMIs posing potential layering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Liquidity provenance pack: (i) a board-approved treasury policy describing the sweep mechanism from EMIs to the Panama parent account; (ii) bank statements demonstrating the end-client collection nature of the sweeps; (iii) a contractual copy of the PSP/EMI terms and settlement cycle; (iv) evidence of actual goods sold (invoices, logistics tracking numbers, marketplace reports); (v) an MLRO-style explanatory memorandum signed by the compliance officer of the client.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the Panama S.A., capital injections from foreign shareholders should be executed in US Dollars via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the entity's Tier 1 Panama account. Compliant routing: (i) remitter must be the actual shareholder or a disclosed loan counterparty; (ii) purpose of payment field 70 should reference one of the following clearly worded purpose codes: 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION', 'REIMBURSEMENT OF CAPITAL', 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN', or 'APORTE DE CAPITAL'; Panama does not operate an official central bank purpose-code registry, but banks apply their internal OFAC/AML checks; if the bank requires a standardized code, use 'CAPT' (capital contribution) on the credit narrative or 'LOAN' for shareholder advances; (iii) supporting documentation must include a notarized Board Resolution/minutes approving the capital injection, a share subscription agreement or scanned share certificate, and a shareholder source-of-funds form if above USD 10,000 equivalence; (iv) if the injection exceeds the account's expected transaction profile, a pre-advice sent to the relationship manager should include the corporate registration extract, UBO passports, and a consolidated group structure chart; (v) funds can be held in the operational USD account; there are no reserve requirements or surrender ratios applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct US-dollar trade settlements to suppliers (China, US, EU) and to PSP settlement accounts; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C at sight or usance) via the Panama bank's trade finance desk for purchases of significant cosmetic inventory from Asia; (iii) SWIFT MT202/MT202 COV for interbank transfers when settling PSP/EMI sweeps of stored balances; (iv) ACH/Wire via the Federal Reserve system for US-domestic supplier disbursements if the Panamanian bank is a US correspondent bank client; (v) corporate procurement cards for low-value office supplies may be issued by the same bank against the operational account. For each outbound wire, the bank requires: invoice, transport/shipping document (or order receipt), and a stated commercial purpose. Currency is always USD, which eliminates FX conversion risk in the payment flow. There are no Panamanian withholding taxes on interest or payments to foreign suppliers on foreign-source purchases; however, supplier payments for services rendered or goods sold in Panama may attract a 12.5% withholding if the supplier is a non-registered foreign entity — for cross-border DTC cosmetics retail, most supplier payments are for overseas goods and fall outside Panama-sourced income.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD is legal tender in Panama; no local FX market exists, so no onshore deliverable forwards or Panama Balboa (PAB) forwards are available or necessary.

Cross-currency forwards (USD/CNY, USD/EUR) may be executed with global banks (e.g., Citi, BBVA, MUFG) through the Panama desk, provided the company maintains an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSA or margin collateral arrangement.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in USD against emerging-market currencies for supplier-side hedging may be entered into offshore under any governing law chosen by the parties, subject to bank's internal credit limits; Panama imposes no statutory restriction on any person entering into NDF contracts.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/CNY, USD/EUR) are permissible as qualified financial contracts under Chapter 53 of the Panamanian Commercial Code; there are no exchange-control approvals, taxes on derivative gains, or mandatory clearing requirements.
OTC FX options on USDPAB or USD/third-currencies are permissible but are rarely needed because all domestic revenue and expenses are USD-only.
Commodity/input hedges for packaging and raw materials (e.g., freight fuel surcharge) are not a treasury requirement under this blueprint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate franchise tax (Tasa Única / Tarifa Anual de Sociedades) — USD 150 where issued capital does not exceed B/.10,000; USD 300 standard where issued capital exceeds B/.10,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; payment via authorized Panamanian banks or the DGI/Tu Empresa online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March for the preceding calendar year; precise due date set by the DGI RUC last-digit payment calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge on the unpaid amount plus monthly statutory interest; non-payment for three consecutive years permits the Public Registry of Panama to administratively dissolve and strike the S.A.; the resident agent may resign, rendering the entity without legal representation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración de Renta, Formulario 201) for juridical persons, including the annual sworn declaration of operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of each year for calendar-year corporate taxpayers (within the three months following fiscal year-end for non-calendar fiscal periods); quarterly provisional declarations (Formulario 155) remain payable during the year if the S.A. generates taxable revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties, surcharges, and monthly statutory interest on the underpaid or unpaid balance under the Tax Code; failure to file enables the DGI to assess tax ex officio, initiate collection proceedings, and withhold Paz y Salvo clearance certificates required for notarial and registry transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation (Declaración de Beneficiarios Finales / annual UBO update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Beneficial Ownership Reporting Module; submitted by the resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual franchise tax payment (calendar-year window 1 January – 31 March per the DGI RUC-digit schedule); any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be updated within 30 calendar days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Executive Decree 267/2021 for late, incomplete, or inaccurate filings; the company and resident agent may be held jointly liable, and the DGI may suspend issuance of compliance certificates required for corporate registry filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies where annual gross income exceeds B/.3,000,000 (US$3,000,000), where the entity is listed or registered with the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores, or where it operates in banking, insurance, or other regulated sectors; below the threshold, a licensed CPA compilation or review is customary but not a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS/NIIF) as adopted in Panama; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para PYMES) is permitted for qualifying small and medium entities within DGI acceptance criteria.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent re-validates and electronically files the identity, nationality, and economic-ownership percentage of each ultimate beneficial owner in the DGI module before or together with the Tasa Única payment. Any issuance, transfer, or economic-ownership change in shares must be reported in an amended UBO declaration within 30 calendar days of the transaction, supported by board minutes, share transfer ledger entries, and evidence maintained by the resident agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share register and transfer ledger (Registro de Acciones)
Minutes book of shareholders and directors (Libro de Actas)
Corporate record file (bylaws, registry modifications, registered-office designation, and UBO supporting evidence) maintained at the registered office by the resident agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – 500 per year for resident agent services, including registered office, corporate records custody, franchise tax facilitation, and DGI UBO filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – 3,000 for a below-threshold CPA review or compilation; USD 3,000 – 10,000 for a full IFRS statutory audit where the B/.3,000,000 gross-income threshold is exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for the general corporate regime on Panamanian-source net taxable income (Impuesto sobre la Renta, Article 699 of the Código Fiscal)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial-source regime: foreign-source income (offshore e-commerce sales, foreign payment-processing commissions, non-Panamanian customers) is jurisdictionally exempt and excluded from the Form 200 tax base. No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 4791 online beauty retail; indirect relief includes the SME graduated-scale regime for small taxpayers (annual gross income below statutory thresholds) and the SEM / Multinational Headquarters regime (Ley 41/2007, as amended) for regional coordination or logistics hubs, which may reduce Panamanian-source exposure to near 0% on qualifying cross-border re-invoicing services. Effective rate on a pure Panama-facing DTC operation is 25%; the blended global effective burden depends on the proportion of foreign-source sales.
